search.default_topic: Hong Kong insurance and financial-services regulation and supervision

queries.template: ({topic}) (consultation OR circular OR guideline OR enforcement OR implementation OR "press release") after:{date_from} before:{date_to}
({topic}) (諮詢 OR 通函 OR 指引 OR 執法 OR 實施 OR 新聞稿) {date_from} {date_to}

inclusion_rules: Include official publications about insurance or financial regulation, supervision, consultations, enforcement, implementation, customer protection, distribution, capital, governance, reporting, or digital operations.
Prefer newly published or materially updated items within the requested window.
Return a concise grounded note for each candidate and preserve native source citations.
exclusion_rules: Exclude event promotion, training notices, awards, vacancies, and routine republication without a substantive update.
Do not claim that no event occurred merely because the search returned no result.

ranking_rules: Rank direct implications for insurers, customers, distribution, capital, governance, reporting, or operating models highest.
Prefer binding or time-sensitive developments over general commentary.
Prefer newer publications when relevance is otherwise similar.
attention_rules: Assess regulatory strength, direct relevance to AIA, and urgency on an internal 0-2 scale; map totals of 5-6 to high, 3-4 to medium, and 0-2 to low without displaying numeric scores.
Use high only when the grounded source note establishes a final rule or enforcement action with direct AIA relevance; otherwise use medium or low.
Use medium for consultations, guidance, or materially relevant developments that require assessment but do not establish an immediate obligation.
Use low for general informational updates without an identified near-term action.
If legal status, urgency, or applicability to AIA is unclear, do not use high.
writing_rules: Use plain executive English and explain the development before its possible relevance to AIA.
Keep factual source notes separate from conditional implications for AIA.
Do not invent facts, dates, quantified impacts, source links, or applicability to an AIA entity.
Use cautious wording when the grounded source note does not establish legal status or applicability.
